html:
SMTO-SKL-0011 — No connected Google account can use Google Calendar

GUID: 82482296-e136-515c-a317-6aeb0d58abb5
Slug: google-calendar-account-missing
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-calendar

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't find a Google account it's allowed to use with Google Calendar, so it didn't contact Google. Your calendar wasn't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, ask SMTO to connect your Google Calendar. Open the Google link it gives you, sign in with the account you want, and allow the Calendar access it asks for. SMTO can only work with calendars of a Google account you've connected and approved.
  2. If SMTO says no Google app is set up, open More options › Parameter Store and check for a Google Workspace OAuth App entry. Ask the person who manages SMTO to add one if it's missing. SMTO needs this Google app entry before it can show you the Google sign-in link.
  3. If you asked SMTO to use a specific account, check in Parameter Store that a Google Workspace Account entry for it still exists, or connect that account again. If the saved account was removed, SMTO can't use it and won't swap in a different account for you.
  4. After the account is connected, ask SMTO for the calendar task again. Nothing was sent to Google, so asking again is safe once an account is connected.

What success looks like

  • SMTO completes the calendar task and names the Google account it used.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste your Google password or sign-in codes into the conversation or the error report.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Google account resolution for a Calendar tool found no eligible google_account record (none connected with the required feature, an explicit account_ref missing from Parameter Store, or no Parameter Store/OAuth app available), so the Calendar request was not sent.

What this means

  • Shared Google account resolution finds no eligible account or the OAuth app is missing, and Calendar execution translates that failure into its account-missing family. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Shared Google account resolution finds no eligible account or the OAuth app is missing, and Calendar execution translates that failure into its account-missing family.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact account reference, shared account candidates and linked OAuth app.

How to fix it

  • List google_calendar.accounts (or the google_account and google_oauth_app records in Parameter Store) and confirm a google_oauth_app exists and an account's granted features cover the operation's required feature. Run google_calendar.connect or auth.google_connect with that auth_app_ref and the needed Calendar features, then retry with the exact account_ref; never pick an account by storage order.
  • Connect a shared Google Workspace account with google_calendar.connect or auth.google_connect, then pass its exact account_ref.

Retry and execution caution

  • Connect a shared Google Workspace account with google_calendar.connect or auth.google_connect, then pass its exact account_ref.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended shared account and app are available with the required Calendar access.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials or private Calendar content in diagnostics.
  • Do not blindly repeat writes after uncertain provider effects.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
